intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a half-day exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years, then walk to the stunning Blue Mosque with its six minarets and exquisite Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide to uncover the layered Byzantine and Ottoman history embedded in every stone.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Immersion
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and exotic spices. Engage with local vendors, practice bargaining, and soak in centuries of trading culture that has defined Istanbul's commercial soul.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in a traditional Istanbul kitchen. Learn to prepare authentic dishes such as meze platters, lamb kebabs, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), and baklava. The class typically includes a market visit to source fresh ingredients, giving you deep insight into Turkish culinary traditions and family recipes passed down through generations.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative and residential heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, visit the sacred relics in the Pavilion of the Holy Mantle, and take a guided tour of the legendary Harem to understand the complex social hierarchy of Ottoman court life.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, gliding between Europe and Asia while admiring Ottoman-era yalıs (waterfront mansions), the Rumeli Fortress, and the iconic bridges. After docking, explore the Karaköy waterfront for a classic Istanbul street food crawl — enjoy fresh simit, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), balık ekmek (fish sandwich), and a glass of çay (Turkish tea) at a local çay bahçesi.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, then take the affordable Havaist airport bus or metro to your accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. The bus/metro costs around 50-80 TRY compared to expensive taxis. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack near the hotel if hungry - look for a 24-hour simit (sesame bread ring) cart or a local bakery open late. Budget: 30-50 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Upon arrival, get an Istanbulkart (rechargeable transit card) from machines at the airport - it saves significant money on all public transport throughout your trip. Cost is around 100 TRY including initial credit. Avoid taxi touts inside the terminal.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Have a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or explore the immediate neighborhood. Walk along the beachfront area to get oriented. Visit a local bakery for fresh simit, börek (savory pastry), and çay (Turkish tea) to start your Istanbul experience the authentic way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take public transport to the Sultanahmet district - the historic heart of Istanbul. Visit the Hippodrome of Constantinople (now Sultanahmet Square), which is free to enter. See the ancient Egyptian Obelisk, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain. Walk around and absorb the atmosphere of this UNESCO World Heritage area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Sultanahmet neighborhood as the sun sets and the mosques light up. Head to the Eminönü waterfront and watch the famous Galata Bridge fishermen. Grab a budget-friendly balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the boats moored at the waterfront - a classic Istanbul street food experience.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery near hotel - simit, börek, and çay. Budget: 40-60 TRY
meals.lunch: Sultanahmet area - try a lokanta (traditional Turkish cafeteria-style restaurant) for a full meal with soup, main dish, and bread. Budget: 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) at Eminönü waterfront boats plus ayran (yogurt drink). Budget: 60-80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes throughout the trip - Istanbul is very hilly. Sultanahmet is easily walkable once you arrive. The Istanbulkart makes transport seamless and cheap. Dress modestly if you plan to enter mosques - bring a scarf and avoid sleeveless tops.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) when it opens in the morning - it is free to enter for tourists outside of prayer times. Marvel at the stunning Iznik tile interior with over 20,000 hand-painted blue tiles and six minarets. Remember to remove shoes and cover heads (scarves provided at entrance). Spend 45-60 minutes exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the magnificent Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya), now a functioning mosque but open to tourists. This 1,500-year-old architectural marvel was a Byzantine cathedral, then an Ottoman mosque, then a museum, and now a mosque again. Entrance is free but modest dress is required. Spend 1-2 hours inside admiring the massive dome, golden mosaics, and layered history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) which typically closes around 19:00 - browse without pressure to buy, practice bargaining if you wish to purchase souvenirs, and soak in one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Afterward, find dinner in the Beyazıt area near the bazaar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café - menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local kahvaltı spot. Budget: 60-90 TRY
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or similar köfte (meatball) restaurant near Sultanahmet - a beloved budget institution. Budget: 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyazıt area lokanta near Grand Bazaar - lentil soup, rice, and a meat or vegetable dish. Budget: 80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque closes to tourists during the five daily prayer times (roughly 5-6 times daily, each for about 90 minutes). Check the prayer schedule in advance. Photography is allowed inside both the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia but be respectful. The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace, the opulent home of Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. The outer courtyards and the Imperial Council building are free, but the inner sections require a ticket (around 500-700 TRY). Focus on the free areas if budget is very tight, or budget for the full ticket to see the Harem, Treasury with the famous Topkapi Dagger, and the sacred relics collection. Plan 2-3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Gülhane Park adjacent to Topkapi - a beautiful free green space perfect for a picnic and relaxation. Then head to the nearby Istanbul Archaeology Museums (Arkeoloji Müzesi), which houses incredible artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus. Entrance is around 200-300 TRY - excellent value for the collection.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the Galata Bridge to the Karaköy neighborhood. Climb the historic Galata Tower for panoramic city views (entrance around 200-300 TRY) or simply enjoy the views from the base for free. Explore the trendy Karaköy streets and the historic Galata neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Simit, cheese, olives, and çay from a neighborhood bakkal (corner shop) - assemble your own Turkish breakfast. Budget: 50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Picnic in Gülhane Park - buy fresh bread, white cheese (beyaz peynir), tomatoes, cucumbers, and olives from a nearby market. Budget: 60-80 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy area - try midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from street vendors, then sit down at a meyhane (tavern) for a budget meze spread. Budget: 120-180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays. The Istanbul Museum Pass (around 1,200-1,500 TRY) covers Topkapi, Hagia Sophia Museum sections, Archaeology Museums, and more - worth calculating if you plan to visit multiple paid museums. Galata Tower can have long queues; go early or late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via the affordable ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Kadıköy (around 20-30 TRY with Istanbulkart) - one of the best budget experiences in the city with stunning Bosphorus views. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) with its colorful produce, spice, and food stalls. This is where locals actually shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Moda, Kadıköy's charming seaside neighborhood with café culture, street art, and a relaxed atmosphere. Visit the Kadıköy antique market (bit pazarı) for unique finds. Stroll along the Moda coastline for free Bosphorus views. Explore Bahariye Street, the main pedestrian shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the European side as the sun sets - the evening Bosphorus crossing is magical with the city skyline illuminated. Explore the Beyoğlu district and the famous İstiklal Avenue, Istanbul's bustling pedestrian boulevard with historic tram, shops, and street performers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or grab something quick before the ferry - simit and tea
meals.lunch: Kadıköy market area - çiğ köfte (spiced bulgur rolls) wrap, kokoreç (offal sandwich) if adventurous, or fresh fish from a market stall restaurant. Budget: 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu area - explore the meyhane-lined Nevizade Street off İstiklal for affordable meze and grilled fish. Budget: 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The ferry between Eminönü/Karaköy and Kadıköy runs frequently throughout the day. Kadıköy market is most vibrant in the morning. The Asian side feels distinctly different from the European side - more residential and local. İstiklal Avenue is lively until late at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) near Eminönü - a smaller, more manageable covered market filled with spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and teas. Entrance is free. Browse and sample freely offered goods. Great place to buy affordable food souvenirs. Explore the surrounding streets of Eminönü for additional local market activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Bosphorus ferry tour - the public ferry line (Şehir Hatları) runs a 2-hour Bosphorus cruise for around 50-80 TRY with your Istanbulkart, passing by Ottoman palaces, fortresses, and yalı (waterfront mansions). This is far cheaper than tourist boat tours and equally scenic. Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı for the furthest point or ride back.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Ortaköy neighborhood in the evening - a picturesque waterfront area with the famous Ortaköy Mosque set against the Bosphorus Bridge backdrop. The area is famous for kumpir (loaded baked potatoes) - a must-try Istanbul street food. Browse the weekend craft market stalls.

meals.breakfast: Near Eminönü - fresh simit from a cart and tea from a çaycı (tea seller). Budget: 30-50 TRY
meals.lunch: On the Bosphorus ferry or at Anadolu Kavağı - grilled fish (ızgara balık) at a simple lokanta with Bosphorus views. Budget: 120-160 TRY
meals.dinner: Ortaköy - kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato) with multiple toppings from the famous Ortaköy kumpir stalls. Budget: 80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (Şehir Hatları) departs from Eminönü pier at set times - check the schedule in advance online or at the pier. This is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. Ortaköy is easily reached by bus from the European side. The area can be crowded on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque, arguably the most magnificent Ottoman mosque in Istanbul, built by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan in the 16th century. It is free to enter and less crowded than the Blue Mosque. The complex includes a courtyard, medrese (theological school), and the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Spend 1-2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fatih district surrounding Süleymaniye - one of Istanbul's most traditional and conservative neighborhoods. Visit the Fatih Mosque, wander through the Fatih market streets, and explore the Vefa neighborhood. Stop at the historic Vefa Bozacısı shop (established 1876) to try boza, a traditional fermented grain drink.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn - one of Istanbul's most atmospheric and photogenic areas with colorful old houses, Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, and historic synagogues. The area has transformed with hip cafés while retaining authentic character. Explore as the evening light hits the colorful facades.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Fatih area - traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a neighborhood kahvaltı salonu. Budget: 70-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Fatih district lokanta - home-style Turkish cooking with daily specials (günün yemeği). Budget: 80-110 TRY
meals.dinner: Balat neighborhood - the area has excellent budget eateries and increasingly trendy cafés. Try a local restaurant for pide (Turkish flatbread pizza). Budget: 100-150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are best explored on foot - the streets are narrow and hilly. This area is particularly photogenic and popular with photographers. The Greek Orthodox Ecumenical Patriarchate in Fener is open to visitors. Balat has a historically significant Jewish community heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque/Museum) - a Byzantine masterpiece featuring some of the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, dating from the 14th century. Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood near the ancient city walls. Check current status as it has alternated between mosque and museum status. Budget 1.5-2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls - the massive 5th-century Byzantine defensive walls that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. They stretch for several kilometers and are largely free to explore. The Edirnekapı gate area offers particularly well-preserved sections. This is a remarkable and undervisited historical experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and visit the Beyazıt area. Explore the Istanbul University grounds (Beyazıt Tower visible from outside) and the atmospheric second-hand book market (Sahaflar Çarşısı) adjacent to the Grand Bazaar - a wonderful place to browse old books, maps, and prints.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or near Chora Church - local bakery items. Budget: 40-60 TRY
meals.lunch: Edirnekapı/Fatih area - neighborhood lokanta with home-cooked food. Budget: 80-100 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyazıt/Laleli area - try a traditional pide restaurant (pideci) for freshly baked Turkish flatbread with various toppings. Budget: 100-140 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church/Kariye Mosque status may have changed - verify before visiting. The Theodosian Walls are freely accessible but some sections are in disrepair - be careful when exploring. The Sahaflar Çarşısı (used book market) is closed on Sundays. This is a less touristy day that offers authentic neighborhood experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) - a quintessential cultural experience. Budget hammams like Tarihi Gedikpaşa Hamamı or Cağaloğlu Hamamı offer the full experience (kese scrub, foam massage, relaxation) for around 300-500 TRY, which is far cheaper than tourist-oriented hammams. Go in the morning when it is less crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy - Turkey's first modern art museum featuring contemporary Turkish and international art. Entrance is around 200-300 TRY. Spend 2-3 hours exploring the collection. The museum building itself offers great Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tophane neighborhood adjacent to Karaköy, known for its historic Ottoman cannon foundry (now a cultural center), traditional nargile (hookah) cafés, and the beautiful Kılıç Ali Paşa Mosque. Sit at one of the outdoor nargile cafés for a very local evening experience - tea and nargile for around 100-150 TRY.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before hammam - fruit, yogurt, and tea. Budget: 50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Karaköy area - the neighborhood has excellent budget eateries including börek shops and sandwich spots. Try Karaköy Güllüoğlu for fresh börek. Budget: 80-120 TRY
meals.dinner: Tophane area or Karaköy - meyhane for meze and grilled dishes. Budget: 150-200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Turkish hammams are segregated by gender or have separate time slots. Bring flip flops and a change of underwear. Tip the tellak (bath attendant) who performs your scrub - around 50-100 TRY is appropriate. The hammam experience takes 1.5-2 hours total. Book ahead for popular hammams.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore - the opulent 19th-century palace that replaced Topkapi as the main Ottoman imperial residence. Guided tours of the Selamlık (ceremonial section) cost around 400-600 TRY. The palace grounds and the ornate waterfront gate are impressive even from outside. Atatürk died here in 1938.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to Beşiktaş, a lively local neighborhood and transport hub. Explore the Beşiktaş market, the İhlamur Pavilion (a small Ottoman pavilion in a park, low entrance fee), and the neighborhood's authentic street life. Visit the Çırağan Palace exterior (now a luxury hotel but the Ottoman facade on the Bosphorus is stunning).
day_by_day.evening: Continue along the Bosphorus to the Bebek neighborhood - one of Istanbul's most upscale waterfront areas. Walk along the Bebek promenade for free Bosphorus views, watch the boats, and enjoy the pleasant evening atmosphere. Bebek is known for its famous badem ezmesi (marzipan) from Bebek Badem Ezmecisi.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Beşiktaş area - traditional Turkish breakfast. Budget: 70-100 TRY
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market area - street food and market stalls, try midye dolma (stuffed mussels) and fresh produce. Budget: 60-90 TRY
meals.dinner: Bebek or Beşiktaş - waterfront fish restaurant for affordable set menu, or grab döner from a quality döner shop in Beşiktaş. Budget: 120-180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. The palace tour is mandatory with a guide and runs on a fixed schedule. Photography is restricted inside. The Bosphorus waterfront walk from Dolmabahçe through Beşiktaş to Bebek is one of Istanbul's great free pleasures.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) - a spectacular 15th-century Ottoman fortress built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople. Located on a steep hillside above the Bosphorus at its narrowest point, the fortress offers incredible views and costs only around 50-100 TRY to enter. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring the towers and walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the Bosphorus to the charming village of Sarıyer via bus or dolmuş (shared minibus). Explore the Sadberk Hanım Museum - a private ethnographic and archaeological museum in a historic yalı (waterfront mansion) with reasonable entry fees. Browse the Sarıyer fish market and the authentic village atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center and spend the evening in the Cihangir neighborhood - a bohemian, artsy district beloved by Istanbul's creative class. Explore the antique shops, independent bookstores, and café culture. Watch the sunset from Cihangir's hillside streets with views over the Bosphorus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or pack a picnic for the fortress visit - buy items from a neighborhood bakkal. Budget: 50-70 TRY
meals.lunch: Sarıyer - fresh fish from the harbor-side restaurants or the fish market. Simple grilled fish with bread and salad. Budget: 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Cihangir neighborhood - the area has excellent budget cafés and restaurants. Try a neighborhood meyhane or a modern Turkish restaurant. Budget: 130-180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Rumeli Fortress is closed on Mondays. The fortress involves significant uphill walking on uneven terrain - wear good shoes. Dolmuş (shared minibuses) are a cheap and authentic way to travel along the Bosphorus shore. Cihangir is particularly pleasant in the evening with its café terraces.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) - take the public ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara (ferry takes about 1.5 hours, around 50-80 TRY each way). The islands are car-free and offer a peaceful escape from the city with Victorian-era wooden mansions and horse-drawn carriages.
day_by_day.afternoon: On Büyükada, rent a bicycle (around 100-150 TRY for a few hours) or take a horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) tour of the island. Visit the historic Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery on the hilltop for panoramic sea views - a 30-45 minute uphill walk. Swim at one of the small beaches if the weather is warm enough in May.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul in the late afternoon/early evening, watching the city's skyline emerge from the sea. Spend your second-to-last evening revisiting a favorite neighborhood or trying any remaining foods on your list. Consider the Kapalıçarşı area for any last-minute souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before ferry departure - simit and tea at the Kabataş ferry terminal. Budget: 30-50 TRY
meals.lunch: Büyükada - fish restaurant near the ferry dock or a picnic with items bought from the island's small shops. Budget: 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Back in Istanbul - treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at a traditional Turkish restaurant. Try kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) or İskender kebap. Budget: 180-250 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands ferry schedule is limited - check times carefully to avoid being stranded. The islands are very popular on weekends and public holidays. Büyükada has several beaches but some charge entrance fees. The island is peaceful and very different from mainland Istanbul - a wonderful contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul - revisit your favorite area or any sites you missed. Consider the Pierre Loti Café on a hilltop in the Eyüp neighborhood, reached by a short cable car ride, offering panoramic views over the Golden Horn and the Pierre Loti Café (named after the French novelist). The Eyüp Sultan Mosque complex below is a significant pilgrimage site. Both are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel to collect luggage and check out. Depending on your departure time, do some final souvenir shopping at the Grand Bazaar or Spice Bazaar - Turkish tea, spices, Turkish delight, and evil eye amulets (nazar boncuğu) make excellent affordable gifts. Restock on any Turkish snacks for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time - use the metro or Havaist bus for affordable transport. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring one of the world's greatest cities. The Istanbulkart can be returned at the airport for a partial refund of unused credit.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast - splurge slightly on a proper kahvaltı spread with white cheese, olives, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, and endless tea. Budget: 100-150 TRY
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Grand Bazaar or Spice Bazaar - soup and bread, or a börek from a bakery. Budget: 60-90 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane - grab a final Turkish snack like a simit or some Turkish delight before departure. Budget: 50-80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2-3 hours before your flight for airport procedures. The Istanbul Airport is large and requires significant walking between terminals. Return your Istanbulkart at an automated machine for a partial refund. Pack any liquid food items (olive oil, honey) in checked luggage. Afiyet olsun (bon appétit) and güle güle (farewell) Istanbul!

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in and settle into your room. Take a short stroll along the beachfront promenade if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack at the airport or order room service at the hotel upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some currency or use ATM at the airport. Store valuables in the hotel safe upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Afterward, take a relaxing walk along the beachfront near the Aegean Bliss Resort to get oriented and recover from jet lag. Explore the immediate neighborhood and pick up a local SIM card or pocket Wi-Fi from a nearby shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Princes' Islands ferry terminal and take a short scenic ferry ride to Büyükada, the largest of the Princes' Islands. Explore the island by horse-drawn carriage or bicycle, admire Victorian-era wooden mansions, and enjoy the peaceful, car-free atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the mainland. Head to a waterfront fish restaurant in the Kadıköy or Bostancı area for a classic Istanbul seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — included with stay
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich (balık ekmek) and ayran from a local kiosk on Büyükada island — approx. 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Grilled sea bass and meze at a mid-range waterfront restaurant in Kadıköy — approx. 400-600 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets to Princes' Islands can be purchased with an Istanbulkart (transit card). Buy one at the ferry terminal on arrival — it will be useful throughout the trip. Check ferry schedules in advance as they vary seasonally.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry or metro to the historic Sultanahmet district. Begin with an early visit to the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Ayasofya), one of the world's greatest architectural masterpieces. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Explore the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and stunning interior at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the Sultanahmet Square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque). Admire the six minarets and the breathtaking interior decorated with over 20,000 Iznik tiles. Afterward, explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople and its ancient monuments including the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet. Enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia — a truly magical Istanbul evening experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish pide (flatbread pizza) and lentil soup at a local lokanta near Sultanahmet — approx. 200-300 TRY
meals.dinner: Ottoman-style dinner at a mid-range rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet — try lamb kebab, hummus, and baklava — approx. 500-700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free to enter but requires modest dress — bring a scarf for women and remove shoes before entering the prayer area. Blue Mosque may be closed during prayer times (5 times daily), so plan around the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace, the magnificent residence of Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the famous Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem, and stunning courtyards with panoramic views of the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to Gülhane Park for a peaceful afternoon stroll beneath the plane trees. Then explore the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex, which houses one of the world's greatest collections of ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot, watching fishermen cast their lines overhead. Head up to the Beyoğlu district for dinner and an evening stroll along İstiklal Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Simit, cheese, and tea at a traditional Turkish tea garden inside Gülhane Park — approx. 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Meyhane (Turkish tavern) dinner in Beyoğlu with meze spread, rakı, and grilled fish — approx. 450-650 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace charges a separate entrance fee for the Harem — worth it. Museum Pass Istanbul covers Topkapi and the Archaeological Museums and is excellent value if purchased on Day 3 or 4. Book Harem entry early as tickets are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı), one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, spices, jewelry, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills — it's expected and part of the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and exotic spices. Pick up edible souvenirs. Afterward, take a short walk to the Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a hidden gem renowned for its extraordinary Iznik tile work.
day_by_day.evening: Take a classic Bosphorus sunset cruise from Eminönü pier. Watch the city's skyline glow golden as you pass under the bridges and alongside historic waterfront mansions (yalıs).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Kokoreç (grilled lamb intestines) sandwich or wet burger (ıslak burger) from a street vendor near the Grand Bazaar — approx. 100-150 TRY
meals.dinner: Fresh fish dinner at a waterfront restaurant in Karaköy after the Bosphorus cruise — approx. 400-600 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Double-check the day of the week before visiting. Bosphorus evening cruises run regularly from Eminönü — short 1.5-hour tours are available for approx. 300-400 TRY per person. Beware of overpriced tourist traps near the bazaars.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı), the ancient underground Byzantine water reservoir with its haunting columns and mysterious Medusa heads. Then visit the Mosaic Museum nearby, displaying Byzantine floor mosaics from the Great Palace of Constantinople.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — considered to have the finest surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world. Explore the surrounding old city walls and the charming Balat and Fener neighborhoods with their colorful Greek and Jewish heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the Balat neighborhood at a locally loved meyhane or bistro. This area is increasingly popular with Istanbul's creative crowd and offers authentic, non-touristy dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish home-cooking at a family-run lokanta in Balat — try stuffed grape leaves, slow-cooked lamb, and yogurt — approx. 250-350 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a trendy bistro in Balat with modern Turkish cuisine and natural wine — approx. 500-700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted access depending on ongoing restoration work — confirm before visiting. Balat is best explored on foot; wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestoned and hilly.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy — a beautiful 20-minute crossing. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), one of Istanbul's best food markets. Sample local cheeses, olives, pickles, fresh produce, and street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Moda neighborhood in Kadıköy, a charming seaside district popular with locals. Stroll along the Moda coast, visit independent bookshops and vintage stores, and relax at a seafront café. Explore the Haydarpaşa Train Station, a stunning neo-Gothic building on the Bosphorus shore.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on the Asian side for dinner in Kadıköy — one of Istanbul's best neighborhoods for authentic, affordable food. Afterward, take the ferry back as the city lights reflect on the water.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Market breakfast or brunch spread at one of Kadıköy's famous breakfast spots — olives, cheeses, eggs, tomatoes, honey, tea — approx. 300-400 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beloved Kadıköy meyhane with cold and hot meze, grilled fish, and rakı — approx. 400-600 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Use your Istanbulkart for the ferry crossing. The Kadıköy market is best visited in the morning when it's freshest and most lively. Kadıköy is considered by many locals to be Istanbul's most livable and culturally rich neighborhood — soak it in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapi as the administrative center of the empire. Marvel at the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier and ornate European-influenced interiors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood. Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) with its impressive collection of imperial caiques (royal rowing boats). Then explore the lively Beşiktaş fish market and the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for window shopping along its elegant boutique-lined streets. Enjoy a sophisticated dinner at one of Nişantaşı's excellent mid-range restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich and tea at the Beşiktaş waterfront — approx. 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Modern Turkish cuisine at a stylish Nişantaşı restaurant — try slow-cooked lamb tandir or stuffed eggplant (İmam Bayıldı) — approx. 500-700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires a guided tour and tickets should be booked in advance, especially on weekends. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Photography inside is restricted.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning visit to the Süleymaniye Mosque, the magnificent 16th-century masterpiece designed by the legendary architect Sinan for Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent. Explore the mosque complex including the tombs of Süleyman and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Enjoy panoramic views of the Golden Horn from the mosque terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding university district of Beyazıt, including the Beyazıt Mosque and the old book bazaar (Sahaflar Çarşısı). Then visit the Istanbul University courtyard. Head to the Fatih district to explore the Fatih Mosque and the surrounding traditional neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most authentically conservative and culturally rich areas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Beyoğlu for the evening. Visit the Galata Tower at sunset for sweeping 360-degree views of Istanbul. Enjoy dinner in the atmospheric Galata neighborhood below the tower.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish döner kebab and ayran at a well-regarded lokanta near Süleymaniye — approx. 200-250 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cozy restaurant in Galata neighborhood — try Turkish manti (dumplings) or slow-cooked lamb — approx. 400-550 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Galata Tower has an entrance fee and can get crowded — consider visiting just before sunset for the best light and manageable crowds. Book tickets online in advance. The Fatih neighborhood is conservative — dress modestly when visiting mosques.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a traditional Turkish hammam (bath) experience at one of Istanbul's historic bath houses such as Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Cağaloğlu Hamamı. This centuries-old ritual involves steam, exfoliation, and massage — a deeply relaxing cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hammam, visit the Istanbul Modern art museum (İstanbul Modern) on the Bosphorus waterfront in Karaköy. Explore its excellent collection of modern and contemporary Turkish art. The building itself is architecturally striking with wonderful water views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Karaköy and Tophane neighborhoods, known for their hip cafés, galleries, and nargileh (hookah) cafés. Enjoy a leisurely dinner followed by tea and nargileh at a traditional Ottoman-style café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Light café lunch at Istanbul Modern's restaurant with Bosphorus views — approx. 300-400 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a well-regarded Karaköy restaurant — try fresh seafood meze and grilled octopus — approx. 450-650 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance, especially on weekends. Budget approximately 600-1000 TRY for the full hammam experience including scrub and massage. Istanbul Modern may be closed on Mondays — confirm opening days before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Edirne (approximately 2.5 hours by bus from Istanbul's Büyük Otogar bus station). Visit the UNESCO-listed Selimiye Mosque, considered Sinan's greatest masterpiece and one of the finest examples of Islamic architecture in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Edirne's old bazaar district, the Bedesten and Ali Paşa Covered Bazaar. Visit the Edirne Palace ruins and the historical Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling arena. Sample Edirne's famous liver (ciğer) and its renowned baklava.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by evening bus. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel to rest after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departing
meals.lunch: Edirne-style fried liver (tava ciğer) with fresh bread and pickled peppers at a local restaurant in Edirne — approx. 200-300 TRY
meals.dinner: Simple, comforting dinner at a neighborhood restaurant near the hotel — try Turkish lentil soup and grilled chicken — approx. 300-400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Buses to Edirne depart frequently from Istanbul's Büyük Otogar. The round trip takes approximately 5 hours total travel time. Start early (depart by 8:00 AM) to maximize time in Edirne. Alternatively, skip this day trip and spend the day exploring Istanbul's Asian shore neighborhoods more deeply.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu, home to an outstanding collection of Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. The star exhibit is Osman Hamdi Bey's famous painting 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Afterward, explore the historic Pera/Beyoğlu district's Art Nouveau architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along İstiklal Avenue, Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard. Explore side streets, visit the historic Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market). Browse independent music shops, bookstores, and vintage clothing stores. Visit the Greek Orthodox church of Hagia Triada tucked among the buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicate the final full evening to a special farewell dinner experience — try a rooftop restaurant in Beyoğlu or Sultanahmet with panoramic city views. Afterward, enjoy a final walk along the Bosphorus waterfront at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Meze and grilled fish at the historic Çiçek Pasajı or a nearby traditional restaurant on İstiklal — approx. 350-500 TRY
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic Istanbul views — Ottoman or modern Turkish tasting menu — approx. 600-900 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Pera Museum is closed on Mondays. İstiklal Avenue is busiest on weekend evenings — embrace the energy. Consider buying last-minute gifts and souvenirs today — Turkish ceramics, evil eye charms, spices, and tea make excellent presents.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take one last walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to soak in the sea views and fresh air. If time allows, visit any remaining sights or revisit a favorite spot from the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on departure time, store luggage with the hotel concierge and make a final visit to a nearby café or market. Head to Istanbul Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of culture, history, and culinary discovery in one of the world's most captivating cities.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — savor it!
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a neighborhood café near the hotel or at the airport — Turkish tea, simit, and börek — approx. 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Istanbul Airport. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute purchases or tips. Consider purchasing Turkish tea, coffee, or spices as final gifts at the airport duty-free. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort, Istanbul. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service or hotel bar snacks upon arrival — try the mezze platter and Turkish cheese board with a glass of local Kavaklidere wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a VIP airport meet-and-greet service for seamless customs and luggage handling. Request early turndown service and a chilled welcome amenity from the hotel concierge before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Take a private guided walk along the beachfront promenade near the resort to acclimate. Visit the nearby historic Princes' Islands ferry terminal area and enjoy panoramic Bosphorus views from the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day orientation tour of the Sultanahmet Historic Peninsula. Visit the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hippodrome of Constantinople. Stroll through the atmospheric streets of the old city with a personal guide who provides historical context of Byzantine and Ottoman heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel's rooftop terrace overlooking the Bosphorus, followed by a fine dining dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast buffet at the hotel — featuring simit, fresh cheeses, olives, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs cooked to order, and freshly brewed Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Matbah Restaurant near Sultanahmet — Ottoman palace cuisine in an elegant setting, try the lamb tandir and stuffed vine leaves
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's signature fine dining restaurant — seasonal tasting menu with Bosphorus views and sommelier-selected Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Keep the day light and flexible to recover from jet lag. Confirm private guide booking through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private exclusive early-access tour of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) before general public crowds arrive. A personal historian guide will walk you through 1,500 years of architectural and spiritual history, from Byzantine cathedral to Ottoman mosque. Marvel at the golden mosaics and soaring dome in peaceful solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Topkapi Palace with a private guide — explore the Imperial Harem, Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the sacred relics pavilion. Stroll through the palace gardens with sweeping views of the Golden Horn and Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus sunset cruise on a luxury yacht, sailing past the illuminated skyline of minarets and palaces. Champagne and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Konyali Topkapi Sarayi Restaurant inside the palace grounds — a historic institution serving traditional Ottoman-Turkish cuisine with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard the private yacht with a bespoke catered menu of cold mezze, grilled sea bass, and baklava for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Early-access permits for Hagia Sophia must be arranged in advance through a premium tour operator. Bring a scarf for Hagia Sophia as it is an active mosque.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. With an expert guide, navigate 4,000 shops across 61 covered streets. Focus on artisan jewelry, hand-painted ceramics, silk textiles, and antique Ottoman artifacts. Skip the tourist traps and visit the most authentic vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) nearby — a sensory feast of saffron, sumac, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and herbal teas. Afterward, take a private cooking class with a master chef at a boutique culinary studio in Eminönü, learning to prepare classic Ottoman dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mikla Restaurant — one of Istanbul's most celebrated fine dining establishments atop the Marmara Pera hotel, offering contemporary Turkish-Nordic fusion cuisine with breathtaking panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pandeli Restaurant inside the Spice Bazaar — a legendary Istanbul institution since 1901, serving classic Turkish dishes in an ornate blue-tiled dining room
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Mikla Restaurant with wine pairing — reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a personal shopping assistant through the hotel concierge for the Grand Bazaar to ensure authentic purchases and fair pricing. Cooking class duration is approximately 3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the ancient underground Byzantine reservoir with 336 marble columns. Enjoy the atmospheric lighting and the famous Medusa head column bases. Afterward, visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts in the Ibrahim Pasha Palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world. Continue to a walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls, the 5th-century land walls that once protected Constantinople.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private whirling dervish (Sema) ceremony at a historic lodge — a deeply spiritual Sufi ritual of the Mevlevi Order, arranged exclusively for a small group with pre- and post-ceremony explanations by a cultural guide.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Asitane Restaurant near the Chora Church — specializing in meticulously researched Ottoman palace recipes from the 15th–19th centuries
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal — a celebrated Istanbul restaurant in the historic Minerva Han building, championing Anatolian ingredients with a modern approach

day_by_day.notes: Photography is restricted inside the Chora Church — check current regulations. The private Sema ceremony offers a far more intimate experience than public performances.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at leisure — indulge in a traditional hammam experience at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built in 1584 by Mimar Sinan). Enjoy the private VIP kese (exfoliation) and foam massage ritual, followed by relaxation in the marble cooling room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus. Marvel at the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier, the largest in the world, and the lavish state rooms where Atatürk spent his final days.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Beşiktaş neighborhood on foot. Visit a local tea house (çay bahçesi) for authentic Turkish tea. Enjoy a private dinner with Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tuğra Restaurant inside the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — Ottoman cuisine in a spectacular palace setting on the Bosphorus waterfront
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar — an Istanbul landmark with panoramic Bosphorus views, known for premium steaks, fresh seafood, and an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the VIP hammam package at Çemberlitaş in advance. Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık and Harem sections — the private guide can arrange skip-the-line access.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private Bosphorus tour begins with a morning drive along the European shore. Visit the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) — a dramatic 15th-century Ottoman castle built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople, perched on a cliff above the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via private water taxi. Explore the charming Üsküdar district — visit the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi), the iconic lighthouse on a tiny island. Stroll through Üsküdar's authentic neighborhood streets and visit the beautiful Mihrimah Sultan Mosque.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by private boat at sunset. Dinner in the upscale Arnavutköy neighborhood, known for its beautiful wooden Ottoman mansions (yalıs) along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy on the Asian side — a legendary restaurant celebrated globally for preserving rare Anatolian recipes, featured in numerous culinary documentaries
meals.dinner: Dinner at Arnavutköy Balıkçısı — a refined seafood restaurant in a historic waterfront building, serving the freshest catch from the Bosphorus and Aegean

day_by_day.notes: The Asian side of Istanbul offers a completely different, more local atmosphere — a fascinating contrast to the historic peninsula. The Maiden's Tower has a restaurant inside if you prefer a unique lunch alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex — three museums in one: the Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk Museum. Private guided tour covers the Alexander Sarcophagus, Ishtar Gate fragments, and the Treaty of Kadesh (one of the world's oldest peace treaties).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beyoğlu district — walk the famous İstiklal Avenue, a vibrant pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style buildings, boutiques, and historic passages (han). Visit the Galata Tower for panoramic city views. Explore the Pera neighborhood's art galleries and antique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private classical Turkish music performance (fasıl) at a historic meyhane (tavern) in Beyoğlu — a curated evening of Ottoman classical music, poetry, and traditional meze.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Galata Konak — a charming café-restaurant in a restored Ottoman mansion near the Galata Tower, serving Turkish home-style cooking
meals.dinner: Private fasıl dinner at a premium meyhane in Beyoğlu — a multi-course feast of cold and hot mezze, grilled fish, and raki (Turkey's anise spirit), with live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeology Museums are underrated and often uncrowded — a hidden gem. The private fasıl evening should be arranged through the concierge for an authentic, non-touristy venue.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Edirne (approximately 2.5 hours by private car) — the former Ottoman capital. Visit the magnificent Selimiye Mosque, widely considered Mimar Sinan's masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A private art historian guide provides an in-depth architectural analysis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Edirne — visit the historic Eski Cami (Old Mosque) and the beautiful Muradiye Mosque. Browse the covered Alipaşa and Bedesten bazaars for local textiles and crafts. Visit the Edirne Palace ruins and the Museum of Turkish-Islamic Art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car. Relaxed evening at the hotel — spa treatment, rooftop bar, or quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Edirne at a traditional lokanta — try Edirne's famous ciğer tava (fried liver), a regional specialty, and the local badem ezmesi (marzipan)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel's brasserie or in-room dining after the long day trip

day_by_day.notes: Edirne is an extraordinary and often overlooked destination. The Selimiye Mosque surpasses even the Blue Mosque in architectural sophistication. Depart early (7:30 AM) to maximize time there.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Istanbul's finest private museums, housed in a stunning Bosphorus-side villa. The collection includes Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and rotating world-class international exhibitions. The garden café overlooks the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Emirgan district and its famous Emirgan Park — one of Istanbul's most beautiful public parks, with Ottoman pavilions and seasonal tulip gardens. Continue to the upscale Bebek neighborhood — a favorite of Istanbul's elite, with chic cafés and boutiques along the Bosphorus shore.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner cruise on the Bosphorus aboard a luxury gulet (traditional Turkish wooden yacht), sailing under the illuminated Bosphorus bridges as the city glitters on both shores.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at Müzedechanga at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum — a celebrated restaurant known for its creative Turkish cuisine and spectacular Bosphorus garden terrace
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner aboard the private gulet — a specially curated menu of cold mezze, grilled seafood, and Turkish desserts, with wine and raki service

day_by_day.notes: Bebek is a wonderful place for a leisurely afternoon stroll and people-watching. The Bebek Badem Ezmesi shop is legendary for its almond paste confections — an ideal gift.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — the grandest imperial mosque in Istanbul, built by Mimar Sinan for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. Explore the mosque, the tombs of Suleiman and his wife Hürrem Sultan, and the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including the historic hamam and medrese.
day_by_day.afternoon: Deep dive into Istanbul's food culture with a premium private street food and culinary tour of the Fatih district — taste authentic kokoreç, balık ekmek (fish sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and freshly baked simit from a century-old fırın (bakery). Visit a traditional helva shop and a historic pickle shop (turşucu).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ulus 29 — a legendary Istanbul restaurant in the forested hills above the Bosphorus, offering spectacular panoramic views of both bridges and both continents, with refined Turkish cuisine and an exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Street food tasting during the culinary tour — a curated selection of Istanbul's most iconic street foods across multiple stops in Fatih and Eminönü
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at Ulus 29 — start with cold and warm mezze, followed by grilled lamb chops or sea bream, and finish with künefe (warm cheese pastry with syrup)

day_by_day.notes: The Süleymaniye Mosque is often less crowded than the Blue Mosque and arguably more beautiful. The culinary tour should be led by a specialist food guide — arrange through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning — final hotel spa session, swim, or relaxed breakfast on the terrace. Optional: visit the nearby Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) — a world-class contemporary art museum in a stunning waterfront building designed by Renzo Piano, showcasing Turkish modern and contemporary art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Küçüksu Pavilion and Beylerbeyi Palace on the Asian shore of the Bosphorus — two exquisite Ottoman summer palaces used by sultans for leisure. The interiors feature extraordinary European-influenced decor and original imperial furnishings.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Nicole Restaurant — an intimate, award-winning fine dining restaurant offering an innovative tasting menu that reinterprets Turkish culinary heritage through a modern lens, with an exceptional natural wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final full Turkish breakfast at the hotel — take your time and savor every element
meals.lunch: Lunch at Karaköy Lokantası — a beloved Istanbul institution known for its beautifully tiled interior and refined traditional Turkish cuisine in the Karaköy district
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu at Nicole Restaurant with full wine pairing — a memorable culinary finale to the trip

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to purchase any final gifts — Turkish delight from Hacı Bekir (founded 1777), hand-painted Iznik tiles, or artisan olive oil soaps from the Grand Bazaar area. Pack in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last Turkish breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow walk along the beachfront for a final view of the Bosphorus. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort with private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure — use any remaining time at the airport in the VIP lounge. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of history, culture, and culinary discovery in one of the world's great cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at the hotel — savor your last glass of çay (Turkish tea)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport VIP lounge or a final börek (savory pastry) from a nearby fırın before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Istanbul Airport, which is one of the world's largest. The hotel concierge can arrange a private VIP airport transfer and fast-track security service. Ensure all purchased items comply with customs regulations.
